newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian NGO flies emergency first aid to former Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Belgian NGO flies emergency first aid to former Zaire.

text.p: Memisa Belgium, a religious non-governmental aid organisation, on Wednesday flew 19 tonnes of emergency medical supplies to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, formerly Zaire, to help restore looted facilities.

"It is basic medical supplies such as aspirins, antibiotics, wound dressings, scissors and microscopes. It is to restock facilities around Kisangani that were looted by the Zairean army in December," director Marti Waals told Reuters.
"It is the start of the second phase of an operation we began in October," he added.
Waals said the first phase of the aid operation had been focused on bringing emergency food and medical supplies to the flood of refugees in and around the northern city of Kisangani.
"The problem of the refugees has started to diminish so we are now switching to focus on the immediate needs of the local population," he said.

The new aid, part financed by the Belgian government, which is concentrating its efforts in the country through national and international NGOs, will be distributed through five diocese around Kisangani.
"These diocese cover several million people," Waals said, adding that many of them had received no proper medical attention for months.
He said the friction between foreign non-governmental aid organisations and the victorious rebel army of new Congo President Laurent Kabila over the refugees around Kisangani had now diminished.
"We can work now. We can get the medical services restarted. We have stayed there and we will stay there working through established local organisations," Waals said.

The aid programme is being run in coordination with the Belgian government whose overseas development and cooperation minister Reginal Moreels is currently in Kinshasa to discuss a five-year bilateral development plan.
Kabila declared himself president with sweeping powers in May after a seven-month bush war that ousted and forced into exile veteran dictator Mobutu Sese-Seko.
Memisa Belgium was created in 1988. It is funded by the Belgian government, the European Union and private donations and works mainly in the Congo, a former Belgian colony.
